## Key facts (verified against legislation and Tribunal decisions)
- The Electronic Communications Code (Schedule 3A, Communications Act 2003) as reformed by the Digital Economy Act 2017 came into force on 28 December 2017.
- Rent (consideration) under the Code is assessed on the no-network assumption in Paragraph 24: land is valued at its alternative use, not its value to the network.
- Benchmark: the Upper Tribunal's Vache Farm decision, EE Ltd and Hutchison 3G UK Ltd v AP Wireless II (UK) Ltd [2024] UKUT 216 (LC), set consideration for a standard rural greenfield mast at 1,750 pounds per annum; rooftop and urban sites are generally higher.
- On 7 April 2026, Sections 61 to 64 of the PSTI Act 2022 came into force: qualifying telecoms leases renewing under the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954 are now valued on the no-network basis (new Section 34A), and Code disputes moved to the First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber).
- Cornerstone v Compton Beauchamp Estates [2022] UKSC 18: operators with 1954 Act protected agreements must renew under that Act, not the Code. The Phone Mast Advice Company instigated and advised on this case.
- A Code agreement does not end when its term expires (Paragraph 30); termination requires a Paragraph 31 notice of at least 18 months on a statutory ground.
- Landlords can recover, on top of rent: compensation (Paragraph 25), reasonable professional fees (Paragraph 84), electricity costs, and payment for access over retained land.
